Benchmark methods & resources

Open a benchmark for its original resources, procedure, selected metric and reported-run scope. These descriptions explain the public protocols; they are not a claim that every company run reproduced the current upstream configuration.

LoCoMoOverall Token-level F1
  • Official code and dataset ↗https://github.com/snap-research/LoCoMo
  • Paper ↗https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17753
What it tests
Tests whether an assistant can answer questions using information distributed across a long conversation history.
Dataset and selected task
The public release contains ten multi-session conversations with timestamps, QA labels and evidence dialogue IDs.
Evaluation procedure
Ingest conversation history, retrieve relevant memory for each question, generate an answer, then compare it with the annotated answer using the QA evaluator.
Metric and calculation
This row reports Overall Token-level F1 on a 0–1 scale: token precision and recall measure overlap with the reference answer. Higher is better; no LLM judge is needed for this selected metric.
Scope of the reported run
All three populated cells come from the latest company report. Sample selection, category inclusion, answer normalization and the exact Overall aggregation are not supplied; the repository’s full dataset size does not establish the company run size.
Score provenance
CoSens: Company run · Mem0: Company run · TencentDB Agent Memory: Company run

HaluMemMedium QA Correct
  • Official code and evaluation suite ↗https://github.com/MemTensor/HaluMem
  • Paper ↗https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03506
  • Official dataset ↗https://huggingface.co/datasets/IAAR-Shanghai/HaluMem
What it tests
Tests hallucinations in memory extraction, memory updating and downstream question answering as separate operations.
Dataset and selected task
HaluMem offers Medium and Long user-centric conversation histories, annotated memory points and QA pairs. This row selects Medium QA only.
Evaluation procedure
Feed sessions through a memory-system adapter, collect stored and updated memories and QA predictions, then run the evaluation suite against annotated reference information.
Metric and calculation
Medium QA Correct is the reported correctness measure on a 0–1 scale. The official suite also evaluates memory extraction and update accuracy, hallucinations and omissions; those are not averaged into this row.
Scope of the reported run
The three values are company-run results in the latest report. Judge version, prompts, thresholds and evaluated QA count are not recorded. A high QA value alone does not establish extraction or update leadership.

MemoryAgentBenchConflict Resolution · Token F1
  • Official code and task definitions ↗https://github.com/HUST-AI-HYZ/MemoryAgentBench
  • Paper ↗https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.05257
What it tests
Tests memory through incremental interactions, including accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding and conflict resolution.
Dataset and selected task
The selected Conflict Resolution task provides facts that change or conflict across incoming context chunks.
Evaluation procedure
Process chunks into memory in sequence, then answer questions that require the applicable updated fact rather than an outdated conflicting version.
Metric and calculation
MemoryAgentBench uses an adapted Token F1 in this company report, on a 0–1 scale. The official repository describes substring exact-match accuracy for its conflict-resolution tasks. These scoring protocols are different.
Scope of the reported run
Only Mem0 OSS and TencentDB have reported values; the CoSens result is missing. The adaptation code, chunk size, task revision, sample count and normalization rules are not supplied, so these values are not official-protocol accuracy.
Score provenance
Mem0: Company run · TencentDB Agent Memory: Company run

OrgMemBenchMedium · Overall rubric score
  • Official corpus and harness ↗https://github.com/JackCGardner/OrgMemBench
  • Methodology ↗https://github.com/JackCGardner/OrgMemBench/blob/main/docs/METHODOLOGY.md
  • Reproduction guide ↗https://github.com/JackCGardner/OrgMemBench/blob/main/docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md
What it tests
Tests organizational memory: revised decisions, provenance, historical belief states, audit replay, justification chains and contradictions.
Dataset and selected task
A synthetic organization with multiple authors, channels and valid-time versus ingestion-time history. The public Medium tier has 443 artifacts and 73 questions.
Evaluation procedure
Ingest the selected tier with a system adapter, retrieve evidence, generate answers and judge them against structured rubric facets. The harness supports both native and shared answerers.
Metric and calculation
Overall rubric score is mean rubric-weighted facet coverage in [0,1], allowing partial credit. This row keeps the company report’s Medium result; its Small result is not mixed in.
Scope of the reported run
Only the CoSens company-run value is reported here. The public tier size describes the benchmark; actual evaluated question IDs, corpus revision, answerer, judge and run count are not supplied by the company report.

LongMemEvalEvidence Recall@10 (%)
  • Official code, data and evaluation ↗https://github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval
  • Paper · Table 3 ↗https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813
What it tests
Tests long-term interactive memory, including extraction, multi-session and temporal reasoning, knowledge updates and abstention.
Dataset and selected task
Public S, M and oracle variants each contain 500 instances, with evidence session IDs and answer-bearing turn annotations. The company report does not identify its exact variant.
Evaluation procedure
For retrieval evaluation, index the history, retrieve the ten highest-ranked memory items for each question, and check against annotated evidence. The benchmark separately supports generated-answer evaluation.
Metric and calculation
Evidence Recall@10 (%) measures reference evidence recovered in the top ten results, on a 0–100 scale. It is not end-to-end answer accuracy. The source does not provide the exact matching and aggregation implementation.
Scope of the reported run
CoSens is a company-run result; Session RAG (V+fact) is a Table 3 paper reference. Retrieval unit, evidence matching, embedding version, query expansion and sample selection are not established as matched.
Score provenance
CoSens: Company run · Session RAG (V+fact): Paper reference

LoCoMo-PlusFactual average
  • Official code, data and judge framework ↗https://github.com/xjtuleeyf/Locomo-Plus
  • Paper ↗https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10715
What it tests
Adds cognitive memory to long conversational QA: use an earlier cue to respect a later implicit constraint, even when their wording differs.
Dataset and selected task
Extends LoCoMo’s factual categories with cue–trigger cognitive tasks. This table selects the reported factual average, not the cognitive score or a combined total.
Evaluation procedure
Build unified inputs, obtain predictions from the model or memory system, then score with the released LLM-as-judge framework.
Metric and calculation
The released judge awards correct, partial and wrong responses 1, 0.5 and 0. This row preserves the report’s factual average on a 0–100 scale; the company aggregation implementation is not supplied.
Scope of the reported run
CoSens is a company-run value. Mem0, A-Mem and SeCom are paper references copied into the consolidated report. Model, prompt, judge and exact sample equivalence have not been established.
Score provenance
CoSens: Company run · Mem0: Paper reference · A-Mem: Paper reference · SeCom: Paper reference

MemBenchParticipation Scenario · Accuracy
  • Official repository and data instructions ↗https://github.com/import-myself/Membench
  • Paper ↗https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.989/
What it tests
Tests factual and reflective agent memory in participation and observation scenarios, with effectiveness, efficiency and capacity dimensions.
Dataset and selected task
Participation data represents first-person interaction; observation data represents third-person information. Released data supports different conversation lengths and added distractor content.
Evaluation procedure
Feed the chosen interaction history through a memory method, answer the associated questions and score correctness for the selected scenario and context-length condition.
Metric and calculation
This row uses reported Participation Scenario Accuracy on a 0–1 scale. Observation accuracy, efficiency and capacity are separate measures and are not combined into this value.
Scope of the reported run
CoSens and RAG (local) are company-run results; MemGPT is a paper reference. The report describes its local RAG comparison as matched, but exact lengths, question IDs, sample counts and scoring settings are not supplied.
Score provenance
CoSens: Company run · MemGPT: Paper reference · RAG (local): Local baseline

Compared memories & reference methods

Exact evaluated versions are not provided in the source reports. Project links identify the original systems; a current release may differ from the implementation behind a historical score.

CoSens

Experience layer with persistent memory and reusable methods. The reported memory implementation is named Friday in the source reports.

  • Website ↗https://cosens.ai/
  • SDK preview ↗https://cosens.ai/docs/#overview

Company-run memory results. These scores do not evaluate the complete SDK or the Learn loop; a public evaluated source revision is not supplied.

Mem0

A memory layer that extracts, stores and retrieves information for agents and applications.

  • Official repository ↗https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0

Latest-report rows use company-run Mem0 results; MemoryAgentBench explicitly uses Mem0 OSS. LoCoMo-Plus uses a paper reference. Platform, OSS and graph variants must not be treated as interchangeable.

TencentDB Agent Memory

TencentDB Agent Memory provides persistent memory infrastructure for agents.

  • Official repository ↗https://github.com/TencentCloud/TencentDB-Agent-Memory

Company-run results in the latest report. The exact evaluated release and storage configuration are not recorded; the current repository may differ from the evaluated version.

A-Mem

Agentic memory that organizes notes, metadata and links, and updates relationships as new memories arrive.

  • Official memory implementation ↗https://github.com/agiresearch/A-mem
  • Authors’ evaluation code ↗https://github.com/WujiangXu/AgenticMemory
  • Paper ↗https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12110

LoCoMo-Plus values are paper references reproduced in the company report. The system repository distinguishes the memory implementation from the authors’ experiment code.

SeCom

Conversation memory built from topical segments, with compression and retrieval over those memory units.

  • Official repository and experiments ↗https://github.com/microsoft/SeCom

LoCoMo-Plus values are paper references reproduced in the company report; they are not a new controlled run of the current SeCom release.

MemGPT

The MemGPT agent design manages a limited context window using external memory and memory-editing tools.

  • Project repository · now Letta ↗https://github.com/letta-ai/letta
  • Original MemGPT paper ↗https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560

MemBench uses the historical MemGPT reference from the source report. The current Letta project is its successor, not proof that this score measures today’s Letta release.

RAG (local)

The local retrieval-augmented memory baseline labeled ragmemory in the consolidated report.

  • Baseline source report ↗https://alidocs.dingtalk.com/i/nodes/93NwLYZXWyEw0OPZiNEg9mBYWkyEqBQm

A company-run baseline, not a separate publicly identified product. The report describes matched local conditions for its MemBench comparison but supplies no public implementation URL or complete configuration.

Session RAG (V+fact)

A LongMemEval paper reference using sessions as retrieval values, with session text and extracted facts as retrieval keys (K=V+fact).

  • Authors’ code and data ↗https://github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval
  • Paper · retrieval design comparison ↗https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813

The 86.2 value is the paper’s Table 3 retrieval reference transcribed into the company report. It is a method configuration, not an independently released memory product.
